content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently underestimate price spikes in the first 10 days of the 30-day horizon.", "Sentiment spikes (positive values) correlate with higher forecast accuracy in the early period.", "Model forecasts show diminishing mean-reversion after day 15, leading to persistent underestimation.", "Forecast bias is most pronounced when sentiment is neutral or negative, especially in the first 5 days.", "Overshoots occur when sentiment turns positive after day 10, causing model to overreact to short-term volatility.", "Model lag is evident when true price exceeds forecast by >5% after day 15, indicating delayed adjustment.", "Sentiment history with multiple positive values within 5 days improves forecast alignment with true price.", "Forecast accuracy declines when true price exhibits sharp reversals after day 20, suggesting model overconfidence in linear trends."]}
